newsitem.title: USA: DeKalb Genetics sees small loss in Q4.
newsitem.headline: DeKalb Genetics sees small loss in Q4.

text.p: DeKalb Genetics Corp, a seed and agricultural company, said Friday it expects a "small loss" in its fiscal fourth quarter due to the seasonality of the seed business and its current business mix.
In the year-ago fourth quarter, ended August 31, 1996, DeKalb reported a loss of $0.07 a share.
The company said losses are typical in its fourth quarter, which primarily reflects continuing corporate and interest expenses as well as swine operating results.
DeKalb today reported higher third quarter and nine-month earnings.
"As anticipated, DeKalb posted its fourth consecutive year of volume and market share gains in the North American corn seed market," Bruce Bickner, chairman, said in a statement.
"The performance of our hybrids continues to drive sales momentum. As we expand our line-up of genetically engineered seed products, we expect to record further gains in the marketplace."
North American segment earnings for the nine months were $44.4 million, up 43 percent from $31.0 million a year earlier. Revenues rose 19 percent to $302.4 million from $254.6 million.
Corn sales volume rose about five percent, reaching a 17-year high.
Soybean sales volume rose to record levels, increasing about 15 percent. Sales were driven by significantly higher soybean acreage as well as continued strong demand for its varieties, DeKalb said.
Nine-month earnings for the international seed business nearly doubled, to $18.4 million from $9.6 million a year earlier. Revenues were $93.9 million, up 19 percent from $78.6 million.
Nine-month earnings for the swine operation were flat at $100,000. Revenues rose 22 percent, to $41.7 million from $34.2 million, primarily due to higher market hog prices.

"Although we are disappointed in results year-to-date, we expect a better performance from our swine operations in the fourth quarter," Bickner said. "We are now seeing the benefits from growing demand for our newer genetics."
